plate_findings.evidence: intense infiltration of lymphoplasmacytic cells throughout whole layers of a medium-sized artery

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Excisional skin biopsy of forearm from cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa case; caption and in-text state medium-sized artery vasculitis feature of PAN; article title is cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa. B: Enlarged view of black rectangle in A showing transmural lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of medium-sized artery in cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa. C: Higher magnification of white rectangle in B showing transmural infiltrate of medium-sized artery in cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa. D: Same forearm biopsy showing medium-vessel arteritis with focal vague granulomatous reaction (arrow) characterized by aggregation of epithelioid histiocytes in cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo from case report titled refractory Cutaneous Polyarteritis Nodosa. Caption and in-text explicitly attribute painful palpable nodules and livedo reticularis-like lesions on lower extremity to the target disease, both visible as erythematous lesions on thigh. Matches two vocabulary findings.

panels.figure_caption: Palpable, painful nodules, and livedo reticularis‐like skin lesions on the right inner thigh (lower extremities) approximately 5 months before initiation of IVIG therapy. Photograph provided by the patient with informed consent.
in_text_mentions: The patient presented with a long‐standing history (since the age of 15 years) of persistent severe pain associated with livedo reticularis‐like skin changes and palpable subcutaneous nodules, predominantly affecting the lower extremities (Figure 1). Symptoms were accompanied by arthralgia, myalgia, marked fatigue, and sleep disturbance, leading to substantial impairment of quality of life.

plate_findings.evidence: necrotizing vasculitis involving all the layers of the vascular walls of the medium and small-sized arteries

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Panel a H&E shows necrotizing vasculitis of medium/small arteries in patient with article-titled severe necrotic cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa, directly matching medium-vessel necrotizing arteritis vocabulary term. b: Panel b H&E from lower wounds biopsy in cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa case shows overlying necrotic epidermis, histologic correlate of necrotic cutaneous ulceration described in title and in-text.
panels.attribution_text: Abousy et al. Burn Center Management of Severe Necrotic Cutaneous Polyarteritis Nodosa in a Patient With a History of Thymoma.. Cureus 2021. doi:10.7759/cureus.13134. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (a) H&E stain, x4 magnification, necrotizing vasculitis involving all the layers of the vascular walls of the medium and small-sized arteries. (b) H&E stain, x4 magnification, overlying necrotic epidermis. H&E: Hematoxylin and Eosin
in_text_mentions: The lower wounds were biopsied, revealing necrotizing vasculitis involving all layers of the vascular walls of the small and medium-sized arteries, exuberant fibrinoid degeneration of the vessel walls, dense perivascular and interstitial neutrophilic inflammation with neutrophilic debris and extravagated erythrocytes, and edema with an overlying necrotic epidermis (Figures 2a, 2b).
